entries.name: Gumbel-Softmax relaxation
entries.definition: A continuous relaxation of a finite categorical random variable obtained by applying softmax to independent Gumbel-perturbed log weights divided by a positive temperature, producing a differentiable random vector in the simplex interior.
entries.identity_notes: Gumbel-Softmax and Concrete identify the same positive-temperature distributional construction: the two inspected primary papers explicitly acknowledge the concurrent work, and their sampling formulas agree after normalizing positive weights. This record covers that shared relaxation and its pathwise-gradient use. It does not equate all training objectives in the papers, the hard Gumbel-Max sample, generic deterministic softmax, or the separate straight-through estimator. limitations: Pathwise gradients can be unbiased for the specified continuous relaxed objective under regularity conditions while remaining biased for the original discrete objective. A correct categorical argmax law does not make the relaxed gradient an unbiased discrete-gradient estimator.

Temperature zero is a limit, not a valid value in the softmax division. Small temperatures can produce sharp derivatives and difficult variance or numerical behavior; no universally optimal temperature or annealing schedule is asserted.
The positive-weight construction excludes zero-mass categories or requires a declared limiting representation. Finite-precision softmax, noise endpoints and ties require numerical policies.
A uniform vector at very high temperature is different from a uniform probability density across the simplex. The relaxation is not generally a Dirichlet distribution.

Distributional equivalence does not imply equivalence of training losses. When a variational objective includes latent log probabilities, replacing discrete states by soft values without a consistent density treatment need not preserve a lower bound for the intended discrete model.

A downstream objective must be defined on the continuous simplex for relaxed training. A model may exploit interior values and suffer a gap when later evaluated with discrete states; neither task quality nor unbiased discrete optimization is guaranteed.

claims.statement: For n≥2 categories with positive finite weights alpha_i and temperature tau>0, draw independent standard Gumbel G_i and set y_i=exp((log(alpha_i)+G_i)/tau) divided by the sum of those exponentials. Normalizing alpha beforehand only adds a common log shift and leaves y unchanged. Each draw has positive components summing to one and is differentiable in the log weights at positive temperature. Holding the base noise fixed allows the chain rule to estimate gradients of a differentiable objective evaluated on this relaxed random vector, under the usual conditions permitting differentiation under expectation. Argmax rounding has categorical probabilities alpha_i/sum(alpha) for every positive temperature; using the same noise while tau tends to zero yields the corresponding one-hot sample almost surely. For fixed finite perturbed scores, tau tending to infinity yields the uniform vector. The relaxed vector at finite temperature is not itself a categorical one-hot draw.

entries.name: Straight-through Gumbel-Softmax estimator
entries.definition: A surrogate-gradient estimator that uses a hard one-hot argmax of a Gumbel-Softmax sample in the forward computation and substitutes the corresponding continuous softmax relaxation’s derivative in the backward computation.
entries.identity_notes: This is Jang and colleagues’ straight-through Gumbel estimator, which retains a discrete forward sample while using a temperature-controlled continuous backward surrogate. It is distinct from using soft Gumbel-Softmax vectors in both passes, from exact differentiation of argmax, from a score-function estimator, and from the broader family of straight-through estimators for other stochastic or quantized units. limitations: Exact categorical forward sampling does not establish an unbiased gradient of the discrete expected loss. The forward/backward mismatch can persist even when the noise distribution is sampled exactly.

The downstream computation must supply a usable derivative with respect to the hard vector, typically through a differentiable extension. A purely discrete black-box reward does not acquire such a derivative automatically.
The derivative of hard argmax is zero almost everywhere and undefined at ties; substituting the soft Jacobian changes that derivative rather than proving argmax differentiable.

Positive temperature and positive finite weights are required by the stated relaxed Jacobian. Temperature annealing, zero-mass categories, finite-precision ties and stability require explicit choices; there is no universal unbiasedness or variance guarantee.
The estimator does not equal all straight-through rules or all Concrete training objectives. No author implementation, learned model or empirical speed/quality result is certified.

claims.statement: Draw independent Gumbel noise and compute y=softmax((log(alpha)+G)/tau) with positive finite weights and tau>0. In the forward pass, use z as the one-hot vector at argmax(y), equivalently argmax(log(alpha)+G). In the backward pass, approximate the derivative of z with respect to its parameters by the derivative of y, while the downstream computation has received z. Thus the downstream gradient evaluated at the hard forward state is multiplied by the relaxed sample’s Jacobian. For log-weight coordinates ell and fixed noise/temperature, that Jacobian has entries y_i(delta_ij−y_j)/tau. Hard output remains one-hot even at large positive temperature, and its categorical sampling law is independent of tau; temperature changes the backward surrogate. This is a deliberately biased surrogate, not the ordinary derivative of the hard argmax or generally the gradient obtained by evaluating the whole loss on y.

entries.name: Ancestral Gumbel-Top-k sampling
entries.definition: An exact without-replacement sampler for finite discrete Bayesian-network configurations that propagates conditional Gumbel subtree maxima through a bounded priority frontier, with a configurable number of parallel expansions and parent-respecting variable selection.
entries.identity_notes: This is Kool and colleagues’ 2020 general ancestral algorithm. It extends the 2019 stochastic beam sampler beyond a fixed sequence-layer schedule: serial expansion is best-first, while expanding the whole retained frontier yields the stochastic-beam specialization. The generic categorical Gumbel-Top-k identity remains a separate mathematical method. Equal output distributions across expansion schedules do not make those schedules or their computational costs identical. All 10 unique hit contents were inspected: neighboring Gumbel-Top-k contrasts, saved review and ledger references, new source leads, and incidental concrete-distribution wording in an older random-search report, not existing candidate records. Exact checkout counts and differences are retained in the ledger. Nine exact AIO CLASS nodes with scoped synonyms/comments and outgoing edges and six full native neighboring records were inspected. limitations: The guarantee concerns finite discrete Bayesian networks with accessible normalized conditionals, well-defined positive support and the specified conditional-max construction. Arbitrary graphical models, cyclic dependencies or invalid zero-mass arithmetic are not silently covered.

The frontier contains disjoint surviving completion domains; after pruning it need not cover the entire original domain. Reusing overlapping partial assignments or sampling a variable before its parents violates the stated construction.

Serial m=1 expansion and full-frontier expansion can have the same sampling law but different work and parallel depth. The paper’s cost accounting includes allocated processor slots, idle slots and potentially unnecessary expansions; it is not a universal wall-clock speedup or a cost independent of variable-domain size.

The retained frontier bound counts entries, not all memory for model states, temporary children, assignments or result storage. Finite precision, ties and numerical stability need implementation policies.
The pseudocode’s access to the first queue element requires an empty-queue guard in an executable implementation. No literal pseudocode, author implementation or numerical benchmark was run.

Without-replacement configurations are dependent samples. The method’s sampling law does not make an arbitrary unweighted estimator unbiased, and it is distinct from Gibbs transitions or ordinary envelope-based rejection sampling.

claims.statement: Given a finite discrete Bayesian DAG with normalized parent-conditioned probabilities, choose a requested k no larger than the positive-probability configuration support and a parallel expansion budget m between 1 and the initial k. Start a priority frontier at the empty assignment, with log mass zero and a Gumbel root maximum sampled from Gumbel(0) or conditioned to zero. Each retained partial assignment represents a disjoint set of possible completions and carries their maximum perturbed log probability. Remove up to m highest-priority entries. Keep already-complete entries unchanged; for each incomplete entry choose an unassigned variable whose parents have been assigned, form all of its possible-value children, and update each child’s log mass with that variable’s conditional log probability. Sample child Gumbel maxima conditionally on their maximum equaling the parent score, using the source’s conditional-maximum transform. Combine children and retained entries with the unexpanded frontier, then keep at most the remaining requested count of highest-priority entries. Emit a completed assignment only while it is at the head of the priority frontier, decrementing the remaining sample count for every emitted assignment. Continue until the requested ordered sample has been returned. The pruning proof uses disjoint completion sets and consistent maxima to preserve the same ordered Gumbel-Top-k distribution as explicit enumeration of all configurations.

evidence.locator: Sections2.1 and2.4, PDF/printed pp.3 and5; Sections3.1–3.9, Equation(18), Lemmas1–2, Theorem3 and Algorithm1, pp.6–15

claims.statement: With m=1 and a fixed variable order the algorithm expands the highest-priority incomplete configuration first and can emit samples incrementally. Expanding the full retained frontier reproduces the layerwise stochastic-beam schedule under the fixed-order setup. The exact without-replacement distribution is preserved across the allowed scheduling choices, but total expansions and allocated processor work can differ.

claims.statement: A globally fixed topological order is sufficient but not required. The next variable may depend on the sampled partial assignment, provided every parent of that variable is already assigned. Such a strategy changes the configuration tree and potential reuse/pruning while retaining the target distribution under the described construction.

native_neighbors.name: Gumbel-Top-k trick
native_neighbors.definition: A categorical sampling construction that adds independent standard Gumbel noise to each category’s log weight and returns the indices of the k largest perturbed values in descending order, producing an ordered sample without replacement under successive renormalization of the remaining weights.
native_neighbors.identity_notes: This is the finite categorical Gumbel-Top-k construction formalized by Kool and colleagues, who credit an earlier observation by Vieira. The k=1 case is the Gumbel-Max trick. It is distinct from truncating a language model to its k most probable tokens and then sampling, from a continuous Gumbel-Softmax relaxation, and from the separate stochastic beam algorithm that applies the construction implicitly to sequences. limitations: The ordered sampling probabilities differ from marginal inclusion probabilities; inclusion is not generally proportional to the original weight or equal to k times its normalized probability. At k=n every supported category is included.

The stated construction assumes positive finite weights and k no larger than the positive support. Zero weights require exclusion or a declared limiting convention; invalid weights and k beyond support are not covered.

Exactness assumes the specified independent continuous noise and exact ranking. Finite precision, random-number endpoints and numerical ties require implementation policies; no software implementation was certified.

Direct finite-domain application perturbs all n category scores. It does not by itself supply an efficient algorithm for exponentially many complete sequences, a differentiable relaxation, or an unbiased sample-mean estimator for arbitrary without-replacement outputs.

claims.statement: For n categories with positive finite weights w_i and 1≤k≤n, draw independent G_i with the standard Gumbel distribution, equivalently G_i=−log(−log U_i) for independent U_i uniform on (0,1). Rank log(w_i)+G_i and return the first k distinct indices in that perturbed order. The probability of an ordered distinct tuple (i_1,…,i_k) is the product over j of w_i_j divided by the total weight remaining after indices i_1,…,i_(j−1) are removed. Common weight normalization is unnecessary because it adds only a common shift to all log scores. This is an exact distributional statement for the specified random variables, not an assertion that the selected indices are the highest-probability unperturbed categories.

native_neighbors.name: Stochastic beam search
native_neighbors.definition: The sequence-sampling algorithm of Kool, van Hoof and Welling that implements Gumbel-Top-k without replacement implicitly on a locally normalized sequence tree by propagating conditional perturbed subtree maxima and retaining the k highest-scoring prefixes at each level.
native_neighbors.identity_notes: This record denotes the 2019 Gumbel-based sequence sampler, not every search algorithm called stochastic beam search. The generic Gumbel-Top-k distributional construction is a separate record. The method differs from independently resampling prefixes at every beam step, ordinary probability-ranked beam decoding, and diversity-penalized beam groups. An earlier search hit about coalition-formation scatter search is a separate title lead, not evidence of equivalence. Full-checkout fixed-string searches included ignored and hidden files in worktree and main, returning 49 and 49 lines respectively. All 2 unique hit contents were inspected: a saved stochastic-beam/Gumbel discovery lead and a search-result title about coalition-formation scatter search, not existing candidate records. Exact checkout counts and differences are retained in the ledger. Nine exact AIO CLASS nodes with scoped synonyms/comments and outgoing edges and four full native neighboring records were inspected. Absence is bounded to this snapshot and semantic neighborhood.
limitations: The requested sample count must not exceed the number of positive-probability complete leaves. Zero-mass branches require exclusion or an explicit limiting representation; an exhausted support is not a source of additional distinct samples.

The exact sampling statement requires consistent conditional subtree maxima and the declared normalized sequence distribution. Independently resampling prefixes at each depth, using raw length-normalized scores, or transplanting ordinary beam early stopping does not inherit that statement.

The paper assumes common-length sequences with padding possible. Variable-length generation requires an explicit terminal/EOS policy preserving the intended leaf distribution; arbitrary forced truncation or nonterminating probability mass is not silently covered.

The linear-in-k-and-length claim concerns the number of model evaluations. Vocabulary expansion, top-k selection, neural-state storage and numerical operations still have costs; this is not a bound independent of vocabulary size or model cost.

The conditional-maximum formula can be numerically unstable in direct exponential form. Appendix B supplies stable transformations; exact distributional reasoning is not a certification of finite-precision implementation.

Distinct complete samples can share prefixes and need not have high semantic diversity or be the unperturbed MAP sequences. Without-replacement samples are dependent, and arbitrary unweighted sample averages are not automatically unbiased.

Appendices B.1–B.3, Equations (20)–(24), supplement PDF pp.1–2

claims.statement: Represent complete sequences as leaves of a finite locally normalized prefix tree, using a declared common horizon or probability-preserving padding of completed sequences. A prefix log probability is the log of its descendant probability mass. Its stochastic score represents the maximum perturbed leaf log probability in that subtree. Start at the root; its maximum may be sampled from Gumbel(0) or fixed at zero as in Algorithm 1, since the maximum is independent of the selected ranking. For each retained parent with stochastic score T, sample independent child values G_i from Gumbel(phi_i), where phi_i is the child’s cumulative log probability; let Z=max_i G_i, then transform each to −log(exp(−T)−exp(−Z)+exp(−G_i)). This samples child maxima conditionally on their maximum being the parent’s T. Pool child candidates and retain up to k with the largest transformed scores, repeating through the declared horizon. Under the stated finite normalized tree construction this returns the same ordered without-replacement sequence distribution as explicitly applying Gumbel-Top-k to all complete leaves. The ordering is by perturbed score, not raw sequence probability.

limitations: The full conditional distributions must be compatible with a proper joint target and be sampled correctly. An approximate conditional draw is not automatically an exact Gibbs step.

claims.statement: Partition the state into coordinates or blocks. Select a block, draw its new value from the target conditional distribution given all other current values, and leave those other values unchanged. Each conditional-resampling kernel preserves the joint target. Composing these kernels in a fixed sweep, or mixing them with fixed selection probabilities, also preserves that target. Later steps in a sweep use the values already updated earlier in that sweep. Exact conditional draws do not make the resulting successive joint states independent.
